newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra to jointly fund three road projects.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra to jointly fund three road projects.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Friday the government had agreed to invest A$45 million over three years in three priority road projects in the state of Queensland.
The jointly funded projects would form part of the A$3.0 billion upgrading of the Pacific Highway, between Newcastle and Brisbane, he said.
"The A$180 million investment in these initial projects will alleviate traffic congestion and driver frustration on the Pacific Highway," Sharp said in a statement.

-- widening the Pacific Highway to eight lanes over a 10 km section between Brisbane and the Gold Coast at an estimated total cost of A$110 million (the federal government will provide A$7.5 million for this project in 1996/97);
-- New bridges to carry eight lanes of traffic over the Coomera River at an estimated cost of A$10 million (the federal government will fund the entire cost);

-- a six-lane motorway between two Gold Coast suburbs, Southport and Nerang, and a new Nerang interchange at an estimated cost of A$60 million (the federal government will contribute A$7.5 million to this project in 1996/97).
Sharp said the first and third projects were expected to be completed by 2001, while the second should be finished by early 1999.
The Australian government is providing A$750 million over 10 years to upgrade the Pacific Highway.

The Queensland and New South Wales state governments will also provide A$750 million each, while also maintaining existing expenditure levels, bringing the total value of the reconstruction to A$3.0 billion.
